Encrypt Behavior

An Encrypt Behavior protects persisted FeatureCell state by transforming finalized pipeline output into an encrypted representation before storage, and restoring it during rehydration. Encryption is optional, opt-in, and operates strictly at the pipeline boundary—after state computation and before persistence.

Encrypt behaviors do not participate in state computation, validation, or transformation. They exist solely to ensure that values written to external storage are protected, while the FeatureCell continues to operate on plain, in-memory state.

Encrypt Stage

The Encrypt stage runs after the Processing Layer has produced a finalized state snapshot and before the Persist stage writes data to storage. During rehydration, decryption runs symmetrically after persisted data is loaded and before any state snapshot is emitted.

Encrypt behaviors operate on the pipeline’s persistence value only. They never alter the FeatureCell’s in-memory state and do not feed encrypted values back into computation.

  • Encryption is opt-in and enabled only when an encrypt behavior is registered
  • Null and undefined values bypass encryption
  • Encrypted output is a structured, versioned envelope
  • Decryption validates envelope shape and compatibility
  • untime encryption failures surface as a VaultErrorShape. Initialization-time decryption failures are handled during state resolution and do not attach errors to emitted snapshots
  • A secret must be configured before encryption or decryption can occur
Initialization-Time Decryption

During FeatureCell initialization, persisted state is restored before any state snapshot is emitted. When an Encrypt behavior is present alongside a Persist behavior, this restoration process includes automatic decryption of the persisted value. The encrypted envelope is decrypted as part of initialization-time state resolution, and the resulting plain value becomes the initial snapshot emitted by the FeatureCell, if such persisted data exists.

This initialization-time decryption is distinct from runtime encryption: encryption applies only to the pipeline’s persistence value after a finalized snapshot has been produced, while decryption applies only when restoring persisted data during initialization.

If no persisted data is available, or if decryption cannot be performed, initialization proceeds according to the FeatureCell’s configured initial state and error handling contracts. This process occurs before the FeatureCell begins emitting snapshots to consumers and ensures that all emitted state conforms to the same StateSnapshotShape contract, regardless of whether the value originated from persistence or from static initialization.

Design Decisions

Encrypt behaviors participate in the persistence lifecycle and are configured at FeatureCell initialization time. Missing or invalid encryption configuration is a fatal initialization error that prevents the FeatureCell from becoming operational. This condition cannot be recovered at runtime and requires a corrected build to resolve.

This split ensures encryption configuration errors are surfaced immediately and deterministically at initialization, while persisted-data corruption does not prevent the FeatureCell from starting with a known fallback state.

Configuration

Missing encryption configuration (Example 6) occurs during FeatureCell initialization. Because the encrypt behavior cannot be constructed without its required configuration, initialization fails and the FeatureCell never becomes operational. No StateSnapshotShape is emitted, and the FeatureCell cannot accept replaceState() or mergeState() calls. Resolving this condition requires a corrected build and a fresh initialization attempt. 

{{`// Fatal Error
Error: [vault] AES256Encrypt behavior requires configuration via setAes256Secret()`}}

Decrypt Failure

Invalid encrypted payload (Example 7) is treated differently because it occurs during initialization-time restoration from persistence. If previously persisted data is present but cannot be decrypted, the persisted value is treated as unavailable and initialization continues using the configured initialState. The FeatureCell remains operational and emits a valid initial StateSnapshotShape derived from initialState.

Encrypt Failure

An encrypt failure occurs when an Encrypt behavior throws during pipeline execution. In this case, the error is captured and normalized as a VaultErrorShape.

When encryption fails, the pipeline aborts the persistence sequence. The candidate persistence value is not encrypted, no data is written by any Persist behavior, and no encrypted output is produced.

The FeatureCell’s in-memory state is not modified by an encrypt failure. The previously committed StateSnapshotShape remains intact, and no partial or encrypted value is applied to state.

The resulting VaultErrorShape is emitted through the error handling lifecycle, allowing consumers and error observers to react, while preserving determinism and preventing corrupted or partially encrypted data from reaching storage.

Design Constraints
  • Encrypt behaviors never modify or replace FeatureCell state
  • Encryption output is not observable as state
  • All encrypted data is treated as a persistence side effect
  • State snapshots always expose plain, decrypted values
  • Encrypt behaviors do not influence pipeline control flow
  • Encrypt behaviors have no effect unless paired with a persist behavior. Because encryption operates exclusively on pipeline output and does not affect in-memory state, encrypting without persistence produces no observable result.
  • If any encryption configuration values change (including the secret, salt, or iteration count), previously persisted encrypted data will no longer decrypt successfully. Encryption configuration must remain stable for the lifetime of the stored data. The encryption secret and salt should be stored durably and committed to a repository or equivalent configuration source to ensure long-term consistency.
  • Very large encrypted payloads may impact memory usage. Persisted encrypted data larger than approximately 5 MB is discouraged; external storage mechanisms should be considered for large datasets.

These constraints ensure that encryption provides confidentiality for persisted data without compromising determinism, observability, or correctness of the FeatureCell pipeline, while also clarifying that encryption is meaningful only when used as part of an output persistence strategy.

Available Encrypt Behaviors
Behavior Description

withAes256EncryptBehavior

Algorithm: AES-256-GCM

Encrypts finalized state using AES-256-GCM and produces a versioned encrypted envelope suitable for persistence. Requires an engineer-configured secret and encryption parameters. During rehydration, decrypts the envelope back into its original plain value.
